## 3-Line TL;DR

- GPT-6 Luna costs **$0.10/$0.50** per million input/output tokens; Sol costs **$2/$10** — attractive rates for repeated work ([OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-sol-and-luna/))
- My impression is that **Sol and Luna offer good value, while Opus 5.5 produces strong finished work** — this is not a measured comparison of task success rates
- Compare **cost per accepted task and review time** — a cheap draft saves less when I end up rewriting it

## How much do the token rates differ?

- These are **standard API rates in USD per million tokens, without caching** — not subscription prices or usage allowances ([OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-sol-and-luna/), [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5/))

| Model | Input | Output | 1m input + 250k output tokens |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GPT-6 Luna | $0.10 | $0.50 | **$0.225** |
| GPT-6 Sol | $2 | $10 | **$4.50** |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | $4 | $20 | **$9.00** |

![Input and output API token rates for GPT-6 Luna, Sol, and Claude Opus 5.5](/images/posts/agi/gpt-6-api-prices.webp)

- The last column is an **illustrative total across requests**, not a claim about single-request capacity or tokens needed for a real task
- Calculate `input tokens / 1m × input rate + output tokens / 1m × output rate` — at identical usage each time, two Sol runs cost $9, matching one Opus run
- Actual retries can add context; output volume, caching, and tools can change the bill — this does not establish a universal two-retry allowance

## Where I would try cheaper models first

- This is an **operating proposal based on price and how easily results can be checked**, not a ranking from a controlled three-model experiment

| Work | Candidate to try | Acceptance check | Escalate or inspect when |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Classification and fixed-field extraction | Luna | Required fields, source support, allowed labels | Fields are missing or values lack support |
| Small, bounded code changes | Sol | Relevant tests, requirements, scope | Tests pass but requirements are missing |
| Design and complex writing | Include Opus 5.5 in the comparison | Logic, omissions, factual support | Polished prose hides unsupported conclusions |

- Valid JSON does not establish correct extraction — compare the values with the original, including suspiciously plausible filled-in blanks
- My favorable view of Opus concerns **the finished output I have seen** — it does not establish superiority across every document or code task

## How I would check whether it saves money

- Choose recurring tasks and fix **inputs, acceptance criteria, tools, and retry limits** before starting — moving the goalposts can make any model look good
- Record **tasks attempted, tasks accepted, total API spend, retries, and minutes spent reviewing and editing** — include failed attempts
- **API cost per accepted task = total API spend / accepted tasks** — zero accepted tasks is a failure, not a usable unit cost
- Compare review minutes separately first — converting them into money requires the same hourly rate and currency. Dollars, minutes, and retry counts cannot simply be added together
- Escalate to another model or a person at the preset retry limit — include that cost in the original task's total

## Community Reactions

- One r/OpenAI reporting-agent user described omissions from Luna — an individual account does not establish a general failure rate
- An r/PiCodingAgent author reported **29 Luna passes across 30 runs: ten tasks repeated three times each** — short, clearly scoped coding tasks, not 30 distinct business workflows
- Both observations matter — finding omissions in a report differs from checking code against an automated verifier

## Q&A (Field Notes)

- **Q: Should I send everything to Luna because it is cheapest?**
  - Start by comparing recurring work with reliable checks — low token rates can hide the effort of discovering omissions
- **Q: Do two Sol runs always cost as much as one Opus run?**
  - Only with the identical input/output usage and uncached rates used in the example
- **Q: Does Opus always write better?**
  - That is not established here — my impression and the proposed workflow need testing on the same drafts and acceptance criteria
- **Q: Can these prices compare ChatGPT and Claude subscription allowances?**
  - No — API billing and subscription limits are separate
title: GPT-6 Luna and Sol: Where Do They Actually Save Money?
description: Low token rates help only if the work passes review. Compare Luna, Sol, and Opus 5.5 through API prices, acceptance checks, and cost per finished task
